{{nihongo|'''Kawara Shrine'''|川原神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Mie|af|Mie-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Mie|ar|ميه (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Mie|az|Mie prefekturası|azb|میه اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Mié|be|Міэ|bg|Мие|bn|মিয়ে প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Mie|cdo|Mie-gâing|ce|Ми (префектура)|ceb|Mie-ken|ckb|پارێزگای میێ|cs|Prefektura Mie|cy|Mie (talaith)|da|Mie-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Mie|eo|Gubernio Mie|es|Prefectura de Mie|et|Mie prefektuur|eu|Mie (prefektura)|fa|استان میه|fi|Mien prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Mie|frr|Mie (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Mie|gl|Prefectura de Mie|hak|Mie-yen|he|מיאה (מחוז)|hi|मिऐ प्रीफेक्चर|hr|Mie (prefektura)|hu|Mie prefektúra|hy|Միե (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Mie|ilo|Prepektura ti Mie|it|Prefettura di Mie|ja|三重県|ka|მიეს პრეფექტურა|km|មីអិ(ខេត្ត)|ko|미에현|la|Mieensis|lt|Mijės prefektūra|lv|Mie prefektūra|mk|Мие (префектура)|mn|Миэ муж|mni|ꯃꯤꯏ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|मिई प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Mie|ne|मिए|nl|Mie (prefectuur)|no|Mie (prefektur)|nov|Mie Prefekture|os|Миэ|pam|Prepektura ning Mie|pl|Prefektura Mie|pnb|ضلع مائی|pt|Mie|ro|Prefectura Mie|ru|Миэ|se|Mie prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Mie|si|මියේ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Mie Prefecture|sk|Mie (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Мије|su|Préféktur Mie|sv|Mie prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Mie|tg|Префектураи Мие|th|จังหวัดมิเอะ|tl|Prepektura ng Mie|tr|Mie|tt|Ми (префектура)|uk|Префектура Міє|ur|میہ پریفیکچر|vi|Mie|war|Mie (prefektura)|wuu|三重县|zh|三重县|zh_classical|三重縣|zh_min_nan|Mie-koān|zh_yue|三重縣|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview ==
Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.

This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic3">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk2">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk2" />, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm2">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk2" />. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk62">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.

The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk52">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.

== Grounds ==
The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk72">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic3" />. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|en|Chamaecyparis obtusa|qid=Q917187|lt=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=Camphor tree}}, {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q796117}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|en|Machilus thunbergii|qid=Q5792073|lt=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|en|Ilex latifolia|qid=Q2706373|lt=Ilex latifolia}}<ref name="sk72" />.

== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic3" />. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|ja|月夜見宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm2" />. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic3" />.

Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk62" />.

== History ==
According to legend, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic3" />. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic22">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}<ref name="sk52" />.

However, during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm2" />. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk62" />.

In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk52" />. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk52" />. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk62" />. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm2" />.

Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk52" />. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk62" />.

== Rituals ==
During the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|de|Niiname-sai|fr|Niiname-no-Matsuri|id|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|ko|신상제 (11월)|simple|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk62" />. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk62" />.

== Access ==
The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.

* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kōtsū}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic3" />. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Q11379036|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic3" />.
* **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station}}, served by both {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central}} {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line}} and {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|af|Kintetsu|ar|كينتيتسو|arz|كينتيتسو|az|Kintetsu Railway|da|Kintetsu Railway|de|Kintetsu|eo|Kintetsu|es|Kintetsu|eu|Kintetsu|fa|راه‌آهن کینتتسو|fi|Kintetsu-rautatiet|fj|Kintetsu|fr|Kintetsu Corporation|fy|Kintetsu Railway|ha|Kintetsu Corporation|hu|Kintetsu Railway|is|Kintetsu Railway|it|Ferrovie Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|jv|Kintetsu|ko|긴키 닛폰 철도|mr|किन्तेत्सु रेल्वे|nds|Kintetsu Railway|nl|Kintetsu|nn|Kintetsu Railway|no|Kintetsu Railway|oc|Kintetsu Railway|pl|Kintetsu|ps|کینکی نیپون ریل پټلۍ|pt|Kintetsu Corporation|ro|Kintetsu Railway|sa|किन्तेत्सु|su|Kintetsu|sv|Kintetsu Railway|th|รถไฟคินเท็ตสึ|ti|ኪንተትሱ|tr|Kintetsu Railway|ts|Kintetsu|wuu|近畿日本铁道|zh|近畿日本鐵道|zh_classical|近畿日本鐵道|zh_yue|近畿日本鐵道|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu}} {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line}}<ref name="sk52" />.
